Rachel / Angela — I reviewed the attached redlines and below are our proposed positions. Quoting Angela for context:

> On Mon, 09 Nov 2026 at 08:12 AM Angela Park <angela.park@medcore.com> wrote:
> > Two urgent items from our side:
> > 1) Liability cap — we redlined to cap liability to $500k for direct damages; need Redwood’s position here.
> > 2) Data routing & subprocessor clause — we need clarity on where telemetry is stored and whether Redwood will permit outbound transfers to a Redwood-managed analytics endpoint (we flagged preferred language).

Legal notes / suggested language:

1) Liability cap — Redwood seeks to keep the cap tied to fees paid in the preceding 12 months (standard for our product). Given MedCore is a large healthcare customer, we can offer a negotiated uplift to fees-based cap OR a fixed $1M cap if MedCore signs a 12-month committed capacity order form. Proposed clause: "Aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, or (ii) USD 1,000,000 where a Dedicated or Reserved Capacity Order Form is in effect."

2) Data routing & subprocessors — we can agree to restrict telemetry export to third parties except where needed for service operation. Proposed addition: "Redwood will not route Customer production data to third-party analytics endpoints without Customer’s prior written consent; non-production telemetry that contains no customer PII may be used for service improvement." We will also provide a subprocessors list and KMS/HSM commitments for production keys.

3) Order Form / PO acceptance — Marissa notes we should not require PO as the sole method of contract formation. Operationally, we will accept POs for billing but require that the signed Order Form is the source of truth for SLAs and capacity commitments. Please confirm whether MedCore can issue POs containing the Order Form ID in the cXML header.

I’ve attached a cleaned redline (Redline_MSA_v3.docx) that reflects the suggested language. I estimate 48 business hours to finalize with internal counsel if MedCore is comfortable with the above positions.

Marissa Cole
